newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan economy needs faster growth - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan economy needs faster growth - World Bank.

text.p: Pakistan's economy needs to grow faster to reduce poverty and create employment for a fast growing nation, a World Bank official said on Tuesday.

"The only way that such large poverty reduction and productive employment creation challenges can be addressed is for the economy to grow at a very rapid pace," said Sadiq Ahmed, chief of the World Bank resident mission in Pakistan.

He told a business conference in Karachi that Pakistan's gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate should be higher than the six percent average during the 1972 to 1990 period because of a population growth rate of about three percent a year.
Pakistan, has an estimated 50 million people living below the poverty line, out of a population of 130 million, he added.

"The (GDP) growth performance in the early 1990s is not very encouraging around four percent per annum. Even more depressing is the projected growth during this fiscal year (1996/97 July-June), believed to be less than three percent."
"A total debt to GDP ratio of 88 percent implies that some 25 percent of Pakistan's export earnings have to be used to service external debt," Ahmed said.
"And some 5.7 percent of GDP or over 30 percent of total budgetary revenues have to be used towards interest payments on total public external and domestic debt," he added.
Ahmed said a current account deficit of over $3.0 billion, principal repayments of around $4.0 billion and fiscal deficit of six percent of GDP left a large gap which had to be reduced.
"Financing these deficits will either create more inflation or add to balance of payments burden," he added.
He said banking and capital market reforms were essential to mobilize domestic savings for financing economic growth.
